title: Limits of Logarithmic and Exponential Functions
topicTitle: Limits of Logarithmic and Exponential Functions
notes: **Exponential base limit.** lim(x→0) (eˣ − 1)/x = 1 and, more generally, lim(x→0) (aˣ − 1)/x = ln a for a > 0.
**Logarithmic limit.** lim(x→0) ln(1 + x)/x = 1, which is the same statement inverted since ln and exp are inverse functions.
**Standard form.** lim(x→0) (1 + x)^(1/x) = e and lim(n→∞) (1 + 1/n)ⁿ = e define the natural base through a limit.
**Log of a limit.** For a positive continuous f with lim f = L > 0, lim ln f(x) = ln L; exponentiate the result to recover the original limit.
**Exam caution.** Keep the argument of ln positive throughout; ln(1 + x) requires x > −1, so only the right-hand limit exists at x = −1.
summary: Exponential and logarithmic limits follow from lim(x→0) (eˣ − 1)/x = 1 and lim(x→0) ln(1 + x)/x = 1.
